S2130.1.1 A configuration option will be provided, via CLI, to make the router act as CPE.
S2130.1.2 The default behaviour will be that the router does NOT behave as CPE
S2130.1.3 G4: By default, an IPv6 CE router that has no default router(s) on its WAN interface WILL NOT advertise itself as an IPv6 default router on its LAN interfaces.

S2130.1.4 G5: Explicitly invalidate itself as an IPv6 default router on each of its advertising interfaces by immediately transmitting one or more Router Advertisement messages with the "Router Lifetime" field set to zero

S2130.1.5 WAA-4: The IPv6 CE router WILL be able to support the following DHCPv6 options: Identity Association for Non-temporary Address (IA_NA), Reconfigure Accept RFC 3315, and DNS_SERVERS RFC 3646.
S2130.1.6 WAA-8: The IPv6 CE router WILL support the SOL_MAX_RT option RFC 7083 and request the SOL_MAX_RT option in an Option Request Option (ORO).
S2130.1.7 WPD-8: The IPv6 CE router WILL support the RFC 6603 Prefix Exclude option.
S2130.1.8 ULA-1: The IPv6 CE router SHOULD be capable of generating a ULA prefix RFC 4193
S2130.1.9 ULA-4: By default, the IPv6 CE router WILL act as a site border router according to Section 4.3 of RFC 4193 and filter packets with local IPv6 source or destination addresses accordingly.
S2130.1.10 ULA-5: An IPv6 CE router WILL NOT advertise itself as a default router with a Router Lifetime greater than zero whenever all of its configured and delegated prefixes are ULA prefixes.
S2130.1.11 L-4: An IPv6 CE router WILL NOT advertise itself as a default router with a Router Lifetime RFC 4861 greater than zero if it has no prefixes configured or delegated to it.
S2130.1.12 L-5: The IPv6 CE router WILL make each LAN interface an advertising interface according to RFC 4861.
S2130.1.13 L-9: Unless the IPv6 CE router is configured to support the DHCPv6 IA_NA option, it WILL set the M flag to zero and the O flag to 1 in its Router Advertisement messages RFC 4861.

S2130.1.14 L-11: The IPv6 CE router WILL support providing DNS information in the Router Advertisement Recursive DNS Server (RDNSS) and DNS Search List options. Both options are specified in RFC 6106.

S2130.1.15 L-12: The IPv6 CE router WILL make available a subset of DHCPv6 options (as listed in Section 5.3 of RFC 3736) received from the DHCPv6 client on its WAN interface to its LAN-side DHCPv6 server.
S2130.1.16 L-13: If the delegated prefix changes, i.e., the current prefix is replaced with a new prefix without any overlapping time period

S2130.1.17 The IPv6 CE router WILL send an ICMPv6 Destination Unreachable message, code 5 (Source address failed ingress/egress policy) for packets forwarded to it that use an address from a prefix that has been invalidated.
S2130.1.18 DLW-1: The IPv6 CE router WILL support configuration of DS-Lite via the DS-Lite DHCPv6 option RFC 6334
S2130.1.19 DLW-3: If the IPv6 CE router is configured with an IPv4 address on its WAN interface, then the IPv6 CE router WILL disable the DS-Lite Basic Bridging BroadBand (B4) element.
S2130.1.20 The IPv6 configuration command will be modified with the addition of a new option CPE. This option if selected will switch on the IPv6 CPE behaviour.
S2130.1.21 The no IPv6 configuration command will be modified with the addition of a new option CPE. This option if selected will switch off the IPv6 CPE behaviour.
S2130.1.22 The show IPv6 command will be modified to show the status of the IPv6 CPE functionality either enabled or disabled

title: The compute node maintains a list of application images that are compatible and available to the device
The compute node must have access to the Allied Telesis Update Server to be able to automatically download application images
Application images can be manually installed on to the compute node by copying them on to the devices flash
Application images generated by Allied Telesis are signed by the ATLNZ build servers
If the image file contains a signature, this is verified and the image is only used if the signature is valid
If the image file does not contain a signature, the image is used but the user is notified they are running an unverified image
S2254.1.16 A application instance can be created on a compute node based on an available application image
The user can select to create the instance using the latest version of an image from the update server
The user can select to create the instance using a specific version installed on the compute nodes storage
The amount of persistent storage available to application must be set before an instance can be started
The CPU cores that the application can use can be set (defaults to all cores on the compute node)
The amount of memory available to the application can be set (defaults to all available on the compute node)
An application instance defaults to be in the STOPPED state
The state of a application instance can be configured (RUNNING, STOPPED)
Changes to the application instance configuration take effect when the instance is started
The user must explicitly request the instance use a new version of the application image
The status of all application instances can be displayed from the device
If the device boots without configuration, any application instances found on the device storage are maintained
The device provides a mechanism for re-generating the configuration from an on storage only instance
An application instance (in configuration or not) can be destroyed (purged from the compute nodes storage) by the user

SER3243.1.201 MAP-E Draft 3 Address configuration
SER3243.1.202 Communicate with NTT-COM JSON Configuration Server with HTTPS
SER3243.1.203 Download MAP Rules from NTT-COM JSON Configuration Server
SER3243.1.204 When request to NTT-COM JSON Configuration Server gives 200 OK reply and rule is good: Enable v6 plus and re-check at random interval between 12 and 24hrs
SER3243.1.205 When request to NTT-COM JSON Configuration Server gives 200 OK reply and rule is bad: Disable v6 plus and re-check with delay of 1min, 2 mins, 4 mins, then every 8mins
SER3243.1.206 When request to NTT-COM JSON Configuration Server gives 403 Forbidden: Do not enable v6 plus and re-check with delay of 1min, 2 mins, 4 mins, then every 8mins
SER3243.1.207 When request to NTT-COM JSON Configuration Server has No reply (or 50x): Do not enable v6 plus and re-check with delay of 1min, 2 mins, 4 mins, then every 8mins
SER3243.1.208 Send DDNS update to NTT-COM DDNS server before communicating with NTT-COM JSON Configuration Server,

SER3243.1.209 Before communicating with NTT-COM DDNS or JSON Configuration Server, check that an IPv6 address is assigned to the upstream-interface that is in the NTT-COM range (2400:4050::/30,2400:4150::/30)

S2425.4.1 show mrp ring will be included in the tech support to provide ring state and config information.

S2425.4.2 (no) mrp ring <n> In global-config mode, enable MRP and enable mrp-ring config mode. <n> is the ring ID. If ring <n> does not exist it will be created. A limit of 1 ring will be implemented for first release.

S2425.4.3 domain-id <uuid> In mrp-ring mode, set the domain ID of the ring. <uuid> is a UUID string of 32 hexadecimal digits of the format <xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx> that defaults to all 'F's.
S2425.4.4 domain-name WORD In mrp-ring mode, set the domain name of the ring.
S2425.4.5 vlan-id <vlan> In mrp-ring mode, set the VLAN ID of the ring. This is only required if the ring ports are in trunked mode.
S2425.4.6 profile (200|500) In mrp-ring mode, set the maximum recovery time profile.
S2425.4.7 role (auto-manager|manager|client) In mrp-ring mode, set the operating role of the node for this ring and set the config mode to mrp-ring-manager if this is selected.
S2425.4.8 priority <0-65535> In mrp-ring-manager mode, set the priority of the MRA.
S2425.4.10 (no) enable In mrp-ring-manager mode, enable or disable the state machine. Default is enabled.
S2425.4.9 (no) lc-react In mrp-ring-manager mode, enable the react-immediately-on-link-check functionality.
S2425.4.12 show mrp ring (<n>|) In privileged-exec mode, display MRP ring settings for a specific ring or all rings.

title: S2254.1.5 Container Services is disabled by default
S2254.1.6 Container Services can be enabled by configuration
S2254.1.7 When enabled, if the AW+ device supports Container Services compute and has enough resource, it registers itself as a compute node
S2254.1.9 The compute node maintains a list of application images that are compatible and available to the device
S2254.1.10 The compute node must have access to the Allied Telesis Update Server to be able to automatically download application images
S2254.1.11 The compute node periodically (every 60 minutes) downloads a list of available application images on the AT Update Service
S2254.1.12 Application images can be manually installed on to the compute node by copying them on to the devices flash
S2254.1.13 Application images generated by Allied Telesis are signed by the ATLNZ build servers
S2254.1.14 If the image file contains a signature, this is verified and the image is only used if the signature is valid
S2254.1.15 If the image file does not contain a signature, the image is used but the user is notified they are running an unverified image
S2254.1.201 On stacked AW+ devices, the application images in flash on the master will be synced to the backup members
S2254.1.16 A application instance can be created on a compute node based on an available application image
S2254.1.202 The user can select where to create the instance based on a selection policy (currently: local, or a specific node)
S2254.1.203 When the user specifies 'local' for the selection policy the node with the controller will run the application instance
S2254.1.204 When the user specifies 'local' and the controller is a VCStack, all nodes in the stack will run a copy of the application instance
S2254.1.17 The user can select to create the instance using the latest version of an image from the update server
S2254.1.18 The user can select to create the instance using a specific version installed on the compute nodes storage
S2254.1.19 The amount of persistent storage available to application must be set before an instance can be started
S2254.1.20 The CPU cores that the application can use can be set (defaults to all cores on the compute node)
S2254.1.21 The amount of memory available to the application can be set (defaults to all available on the compute node)
S2254.1.22 An application instance defaults to be in the STOPPED state
S2254.1.23 The state of a application instance can be configured (RUNNING, STOPPED)
S2254.1.24 Changes to the application instance configuration take effect when the instance is started
S2254.1.25 The user must explicitly request the instance use a new version of the application image
S2254.1.26 The status of all application instances can be displayed from the device
S2254.1.27 If the device boots without configuration, any application instances found on the device storage are maintained
S2254.1.28 The device provides a mechanism for re-generating the configuration from an on storage only instance
S2254.1.29 An application instance (in configuration or not) can be destroyed (purged from the compute nodes storage) by the user
S2254.1.30 An application instance can be configured to have one or more network interfaces
S2254.1.31 Each network interface appears, to the instance, as an Ethernet interface (eth0, eth1, ...)
S2254.1.32 Instances can be attached to the real world using one of; Virtual, Shared, or Physical network attachment
S2254.1.33 Virtually attached interfaces will be a enslaved to the global vlan-aware bridge (br0) on the host
S2254.1.34 Virtual network attachment is available on the AR4050S and Appliance Box only
S2254.1.35 Shared interfaces share the interface of the host using a unique MAC address for the Instance
S2254.1.36 Instances can share VLAN interfaces on AW+ products only
S2254.1.37 Physically attached interfaces are transferred into the Instances namespace (no longer visible on the host)
S2254.1.38 Instances can take ownership of ETH interfaces on the Appliance Box only
S2254.1.39 A fixed MAC address can optionally be assigned to each network interface
S2254.1.40 The instance can be configured to run DHCP (if it supports it) on its network interface
S2254.1.41 An IPv4 address can be statically assigned to the instances Ethernet interface
S2254.1.42 An IPv4 gateway address can be assigned to the instances Ethernet interface
S2254.1.43 Static IPv4 configuration and DHCP configuration is mutually exclusive for an interface
S2254.1.44 If an IPv4 address is configured and a MAC address is not, the MAC address is generated from the IP address in the format 02:42:IP1:IP2:IP3:IP4
S2254.1.45 If a MAC address is not available from configuration, a random MAC address is used
S2254.1.46 Host side data plane attachment can be configured by specifying the VLAN ID packets to/from the interface belongs to
S2254.1.47 All instance interfaces are attached to the global bridge "br0" on the compute node with VLAN filtering for the specified VID
S2254.1.48 One or more IPv4 DNS servers can be configured for the instance to use
S2254.1.49 On the AR4050S container virtual networks can be accessed via br0 sub-interfaces (e.g. br0.2 for VID 2)
S2254.1.50 On the AR4050S other interfaces can be enslaved to the global bridge based on VID
S2254.1.51 Ethernet interfaces enslaved to the global bridge are untagged members of VID1 and tagged members of all other VLANs (2..4094)
S2254.1.52 VLAN interfaces enslaved to the global bridge are untagged members of the VLANs actual VID only
S2254.1.53 Packets IP routed to/from the Instance by the host have all UTM functionality applied to them (via iptables hooks)
S2254.1.54 Packets received on the hosts physical interfaces are always processed by stream features
S2254.1.55 Packets transmitted by the Instance and bridged to the physical network via the host are not processed by stream features (unless 'l3-filtering' on the bridge is enabled)
S2254.1.56 Packets transmitted by the Instance over a shared physical interface are not processed by any UTM features
S2254.1.57 Packets received or transmitted by the Instance over a Instance owned physical interface are not processed by any UTM features
S2254.1.84 Enable Container Services
S2254.1.85 Display the status of available compute nodes (including the application images available to those nodes)
S2254.1.86 Create/start/stop/restore/destroy application instances on available compute nodes
S2254.1.87 Display the status of installed applications
S2254.1.88 Display the system log of an application instance (if the instance uses a compatible logging system)
S2254.1.91 Log messages for a change in state of an application instance
S2254.1.106 All externally accessible management must be secured and authenticated
S2254.1.107 Passwords must not be visible in clear-text in any UI used to configure Container Services
S2254.1.108 Application images generated by Allied Telesis are signed to ensure they are valid
S2254.1.109 Applications have their own root file system and have no access the host's file system
S2254.1.110 Applications can be prevented from using all of the hosts RAM, Storage and CPUs

title: DNS64 intercepts A records and sends the client a AAAA record with a generated IPv6 address than can be translated to the given IPv4 address
The tunnel mode map4to6 and 4to6-mapping configuration allow for both NAT46 and NAT64.
S2954.1.1 NAT46 functionality will be unchanged.
S2954.1.2 As with NAT46, tunnel mode map4to6 will be used for NAT64.
S2954.1.3 As with NAT46, 4to6mapping configuration will be used by the tunnel.
S2954.1.4 A single IPv6 /96 subnet can be configured to map the whole external (Internet) IPv4 address range to.
S2954.1.5 A single IPv6 /96 subnet can be configured to use on the IPv6 only side as the network to be translated.
S2954.1.6 Translations will be static
S2954.1.7 Translation algorithm will be RFC 6052.
S2954.1.8 IPv6 traffic routed to the tunnel will be translated to IPv4 using the configured mapping ranges.
S2954.1.9 IP traffic routed to the tunnel will be translated to IPv6 using the configured mapping ranges.
S2954.1.10 ICMPv6 routed to the tunnel will be translated to ICMP using configured mappings.
S2954.1.11 ICMP routed to the tunnel will be translated to ICMPv6.
S2954.1.12 Read DNS AAAA requests and send both a DNS A request and AAAA request if possible.
S2954.1.13 Translate received A record into a AAAA record to return to IPv6 only network.
S2954.1.14 DNS64 will use a 4to6mapping configuration to chose the address to send in the AAAA record.
S2954.1.15 ip dns forwarding dns64 <4to6mapping>

S2923.1.1 A IE340 fitted with STM32 MPU and BCM59131 PSE controllers will use Broadcom PoE firmware V1.3.0 B15.
S2923.1.2 A IE340 fitted with GD32 MPU and BCM59131 PSE controllers will use Broadcom PoE firmware V5.0.0 B14.
S2923.1.3 If the application firmware version and build number doesn't match the expected values, the correct firmware will be flashed at startup.
S2923.1.4 If no application image is installed, AW+ will install the correct application firmware that is supported by the AW+ version.
S2923.1.5 The device will start up without errors.
S2923.1.6 The device will show correct information (valid available power, etc) in show power-inline.

S2923.1.7 The device will show correct information in show platform power-inline, most importantly "DevID e131 SwVer 130 [...] ExtSwVer 0f" (for STM32) or "DevID e1ff SwVer 500 [...] ExtSwVer 0e" (for GD32).
S2923.1.8 PDs up to class 8/90W can be powered on all ports.
S2923.1.9 Firmware can be erased with start-shell command poe_fw -e, and firmware will be flashed during the next startup.
S2923.1.10 The GD32 MCU will use I2C address 0x22.
S2923.1.11 The STM32 MCU will use I2C address 0x23.
S2923.1.12 The size of the complete firmware image (with BootROM) is 64KB for V130B15 and 99KB for V500B14. These are already included in AW+ prior to this project.

S2923.1.13 Whenever a firmware update takes place (e.g. new firmware included in a new AW+ release), the MCU will be reset and HANP functionality will be interrupted. This is the same as current existing behaviour on HANP-capable PoE switches.
S2923.3.1 new device ID and version: "DevID e131 SwVer 130 [...] ExtSwVer 0f" for STM32+BCM59131.
S2923.3.2 new device ID and version: "DevID e1ff SwVer 500 [...] ExtSwVer 0e" for GD32+BCM59131.
S2923.3.3 For V130B15 only: on an unconnected port, the port status field "Err" will be "06" instead of previous "01" (meaning Open Circuit).
S2923.3.4 For V130B15 only: on an unconnected port, the port status field "Class" will be "06" instead of the previous "01".
S2923.3.5 For V130B15 only: on an unconnected port, the port status MPSS bitmap will be "00" instead of the previous "ff".

ER-6397.1.7 If a LAN switchport has been updated to work as a WAN switchport. show system mac will display the newly assigned MAC and interface.
ER-6397.1.8 The ARX200S must be rebooted before the change to or from WAN mode takes effect.
ER-6397.1.9 Bridging (and bridge commands) are not supported on the WAN switchport.

S3132.1.1 The feature will allow flow identification, time-stamping and counting for each identified flow.
S3132.1.2 The feature will allow an Observation point to be configured on a port to monitor Ingress traffic
The feature will allow the AW+ device to run as a IPFIX device which will integrate a Observation point, Metering Process and a IPFIX Exporter
S3132.1.4 The feature will allow integration of the third party CESNET IPFIXPROBE to run as a IPFIX Exporter
S3132.1.5 The feature will allow connectivity(tcp/udp) from the IPFIX Exporter to the IPFIX Collector(Ex CESNET IPFIXCOL2) to be configured. The Collector is external to AW+
S3132.1.6 The feature will support inactive timeout which is the frequency of inactive flow records that are exported by IPFIXPROBE default to 30 seconds.
S3132.1.7 The feature will generate a 64bit Observation Domain ID to identify the IPFIXPROBE exporter to the Collector from the AW+ device UUID MD5 hash.
The feature will be supported on switchports, SFP/SFP+ ports, static aggregators and member switchports of the dynamic aggregators.
The feature will support aging of identified flows.
The feature will match on IPv4/IPv6 traffic and copy the unidentified traffic to the CPU for flow identification on the flow monitored interfaces.
S3132.1.11 The feature will be supported on a stack. Stack failover support:

S3132.1.12 The feature will allow flow classification for IPv4 packets based on any or all of the following information {IPv4 Source Address, IPv4 Destination Address, IP protocol (TCP/UDP), Source port, Destination port and DSCP}

S3132.1.13 The feature will allow flow classification for IPv6 packets based on any or all of the following information {Full IPv6 Source Address, Full IPv6 Destination Address, IP protocol (TCP/UDP), Source port, Destination port and DSCP}
S3132.1.14 The feature will support Exact Match Table instead of TCAM with IPFIX Flow auto-learning via IPFIX firmware support for Gen 6.1 devices

S3132.1.15 The feature will add Exact Match Rule(Counting entry) to the Exact Match Table for each identified flow. The packets received further will then be counted by the silicon based on this counting entry.
S3132.1.16  The Exact Match rules configured may get affected by other higher priority ACLs configured globally or on the interface

S3132.1.17 The feature will support a dedicated table for IPFIX flows which allows these devices to have many flows. The table mentioned below provides a best estimate for actual number of flows supported on each device.
S3132.1.18 The feature will allow flow classification for IPv6 packets based on full IPv6 Source Address on x530 target when "platform hwfilter-size basic" is configured.
S3132.1.19 The feature will not be supported on the dynamic aggregator and member switchports of the static aggregators.
S3132.1.22 show platform exactMatchTable utilization brief will be included in the tech support output for Gen 6.1 devices.
S3132.1.23 (no |) service flow will enable or disable flow identification on the device.

S3132.1.24 (no |) flow record <NAME> command defines a flow record with match IPv4/IPv6/L4 fields to match incoming traffic and identify unique flows. IPv4 and IPv6 matches can not be configured together under a single record. Maximum 60 flow record

S3132.1.25 (no |) flow exporter <NAME> command will configure access to a flow Collector. Only one exporter could be configured as we only have one exporter type as ipfix, In future this can be extended to multiple exporters of different exporter ty

S3132.1.26 (no |) flow monitor <NAME> command will define a monitor to monitor traffic and send it to a exporter. The flow record for IPv4 and IPv6, and the exporter is applied to the monitor. Maximum 60 monitors could be created.

S3132.1.27 (no |) flow monitor-map <NAME> will enable or disable flow monitoring on an interface. The monitor should be configured with flow record and exporter before applying it to the interface. Only one monitor can be applied on an interface.

S3132.1.29 show flow record (NAME|) will provide information for the flow record.
S3132.1.30 show flow exporter (NAME|) will provide information for the exporter.
S3132.1.31 show flow monitor (NAME|) will provide information and statistics for a monitor.

ER6925.1.5 Capability type will have a type of enum, which takes on the value of one of the currently defined capabilities.
ER6925.1.6 Initial capability will be the ability of the interface to be a layer 3 interface.
ER6925.1.7 absence of a value for the capability will be taken as "undefined".
ER6925.1.8 The interface library will provide APIs for setting the capabilities, but will also set capabilities to their default value when the interface is created or updated.

S3156.1.1 Peer-to-Peer measurement mode will be supported.
S3156.1.2 Event messages will use UDP port 319.
S3156.1.3 General messages will use UDP port 320.
S3156.1.4 The Domain number will remain as 0.
S3156.1.5 Hardware time stamping will be used on the IE340, IE360 & IE560.
S3156.1.6 Configuration of multiple modes can be supported. (L2 and UDP IPV4 and UDP IPv6.)
S3156.2.1 The PTP Boundary Clock is not supported.
S3156.2.2 The PTP Master Clock is not supported.
S3156.2.3 The PTP Slave Clock is not supported.
S3156.2.4 Configuration of a non-default PTP UDP port is not supported.
S3156.2.5 PTP peer-to-peer will not be supported on VCS.
S3156.3.1 New show commands may be added to Tech Support
S3156.3.2 A new ptp-class NAME modal command will be supported
S3156.3.3 Multiple ptp-class configurations can be configured, and applied to ports.

S3156.3.4 When the modal command is selected it will display <config-ptp-class>, "delay-mechanism (e2e | p2p)", "step-type (onestep | twostep)", "transport-type ethernet", "transport-type udp ipv4" and "transport-type udp ipv6" can be configured
S3156.3.5 A maximum of 5 ptp-class configuration can be created and saved.
S3156.3.6 Clock type transparent is the only supported type. No CLI is required. The show commands will display Clock type
S3156.3.7 clock-port NAME will be supported on switchport interfaces, The NAME needs to match a ptp-class NAME configuration
S3156.3.8 Only one clock-port NAME will be supported on each switchport interface.
S3156.3.9 The existing clock-port command will continue to work, It will default to the global ptk-clk configuration.
S3156.3.14 Unsupported PTP commands will be removed from the CLI.
S3156.3.15 The new CLI must be used for PTP Peer to Peer configuration
S3156.3.16 Commands to be removed are boundary, ordinary, p2p and twostep
S3156.3.17 A deprecated CLI message will be printed with the existing CLI to encourage users to update. See CLI_Deprecation
S3156.3.18 The global configuration command ptp-clk transparent transport-type ethernet delay-mechanism e2e step-type onestep will display a deprecated message
S3156.3.19 The global configuration command ptp-clk transparent transport-type udp v4 delay-mechanism e2e step-type onestep will display a deprecated message
S3156.3.20 The global configuration command ptp-clk transparent transport-type udp v6 delay-mechanism e2e step-type onestep will display a deprecated message
S3156.3.21 The switchport interface command clock-port will display a deprecated message
S3156.3.22 Consequently show ptp port display will be updated and show ptp port (IFNAME|) will be supported.
S3156.3.31 show ptp data has been removed. Due to no longer having a global configuration this information is better accessed via show ptp clock and show ptp port
S3156.3.10 show ptp class will be implemented in user exec mode to display configurations and list port.
S3156.3.11 When a port is configured to use Peer-to-Peer delay mechanism, the Peer Mean Path Delay will be available. i.e. 1234 ns.
S3156.3.12 show ptp brief will be implemented in user exec mode to display port configuration and activity.
S3156.3.13 show ptp counters will display the Linux PTP counters for timekeeping and synchronization.
S3156.4.1 A log notice stating "net devices is enabled in the kernel" at startup will be implemented

S3169.1.1 Support configuring a trustpoint to use EST as it's enrollment method.
S3169.1.2 Trustpoints using EST must have an EST URL configured.
S3169.1.3 Trustpoints using EST can optionally have a username and password configured. If present this will be used for HTTP basic authentication.
S3169.1.4 Trustpoints using EST will be authenticated by retrieving the CA from the server at the URL over EST.
S3169.1.5 Trustpoints using EST will be enrolled by their certificate signed by the server at the URL over EST.
S3169.1.6 Trustpoints using EST will periodically refresh their certificates by the server at the URL over EST.
S3169.1.7 Certificates will be refreshed 3 days before expiry, or when 90% of the valid duration has expired, whichever is later.
S3169.1.8 Certificates in the system store can be added to with the "crypto pki import default-system" command.
S3169.1.9 Custom certificates in the default-system store can be removed with the "no crypto pki certificate default-system" command.
S3169.1.10 The default-system store will be used for authenticating the TLS (HTTPS) connection to the EST server.
S3169.1.11 Command to enable EST enrollment enrollment est
S3169.1.12 Command to set the URL to be used by EST enrollment est-url URL
S3169.1.13 Command to set the username to be used for HTTP basic authentication during EST enrollment est-username WORD
S3169.1.14 Command to set the password to be used for HTTP basic authentication during EST enrollment est-password WORD
S3169.1.15 Existing show command will be adjusted to also display EST information used by a trustpoint show crypto pki trustpoint
S3169.1.16 A log will be recorded when a CA certificate is retrieved via EST.
S3169.1.17 A log will be recorded when a certificate is signed via EST.

S3170.1.1 Support configuring a trustpoint to use SCEP as it's enrollment method.
S3170.1.2 Trustpoints using SCEP must have an SCEP URL configured. This can be HTTP or HTTPS.
S3170.1.3 Trustpoints using SCEP can optionally have a challenge password configured. If present this will be used in the CSR.
S3170.1.4 Trustpoints using SCEP will be authenticated by retrieving the CA from the server at the URL over SCEP.
S3170.1.5 Trustpoints using SCEP will be enrolled by their certificate signed by the server at the URL over SCEP.
S3170.1.6 Trustpoints using SCEP will periodically refresh their certificates by the server at the URL over SCEP.
S3170.1.7 Certificates will be refreshed 3 days before expiry, or when 90% of the valid duration has expired, whichever is later.
S3170.1.8 If a PENDING response is received from the SCEP server then we will poll every 5 minutes for a successful response.
S3170.1.9 The default-system store will be used for authenticating the TLS (HTTPS) connection to the SCEP server.
S3170.1.10 Command to enable SCEP enrollment enrollment scep
S3170.1.11 Command to set the URL to be used by SCEP enrollment scep-url URL
S3170.1.12 Command to set the password to be used for the password challenge during SCEP enrollment scep-password WORD
S3170.1.13 Existing show command will be adjusted to also display SCEP information used by a trustpoint show crypto pki trustpoint
S3170.1.14 A notice level log will be recorded when the timer is started to re-enroll the trustpoint with SCEP "Re-enrollment timer started for TPNAME".
S3170.1.15 A notice level log will be recorded when the trustpoint is re-enrolled with SCEP "Successfully re-enrolled trust point TPNAME".

S3206.1.1 Current AW+ mail commands operate identically to before, but now using a new mail client
S3206.1.2 OAuth 2.0 The ability to set OAuth2 as the authentication method will be implemented in 5.5.5-2.x
S3206.2.1 OAUTH2 for providers other than Google and Microsoft will not be supported.
S3206.2.2 Automatically receiving auth code via redirect URI is not supported. The user will have to manually copy the code.
S3206.3.1 the command mail smtpserver authentication oauth2 will be implemented to support OAuth 2.0 authentication. This command enters a new SMTP_OAUTH cli mode, where OAUTH info can be specified.

S3206.3.2 the command username USERNAME provider google client-id CLIENTID client-secret CLIENTSECRET will be implemented to support OAuth 2.0 authentication for google. This command is entered from the smtp-oauth cli mode.

S3206.3.3 the command username USERNAME provider microsoft client-id CLIENTID tenant-id TENANTID client-secret CLIENTSECRET will be implemented to support OAuth 2.0 authentication for Microsoft. This command is entered from the smtp-oauth cli mode

S3206.3.4 the command oauth2-type (xoauth2 │ oauthbearer) will be implemented to allow selecting which type of oauth2 to use as mail provider support may differ. The default shall be xoauth2 as that is supported by both Google and Microsoft.
S3206.3.5 the command redirect-uri REDIRECT_URI will be implemented to allow overwriting the default of localhost.

S3206.3.6 the HIDDEN command (no) mail smtpserver tls disable-cert-check will disable(or re-enable) TLS Peer Verification for testing purposes, allowing the client to send mail over TLS (smtps/starttls) to an SMTP server using a self-signed certificate.

S3206.3.7 the command show mail oauth2 url will be implemented.This command will use the information provided code and attempt to obtain a refresh token from the OAUTH providers API. This completes OAUTH2 setup and authorities the device.
S3206.3.8 the command mail oauth2 code CODE will be implemented.
S3206.3.9 The following configuration commands will be updated to use new mail client. With commands operating the same as before.
S3206.3.10 The following show commands will be update to use new mail client
S3206.3.11 If oauth2 authentication is selected, show mail will additionally print the OAUTH provider in the mail settings

S3236.1.3 The ETS Configuration TLV "CBS" bit will always be set to 0, indicating this device does not support credit-based-shaper.
S3236.1.4 The ETS Configuration TLV "Max TCs" bit will always be set to 0, indicating this device supports ETS on 8 traffic classes.
S3236.1.5 The ETS Configuration TLV "Priority Assignment Table" will be populated with the cos-queue map as configured by mls qos map cos-queue.
S3236.1.6 The ETS Configuration TLV "TC Bandwidth Table" will be populated based on the scheduler-set configuration of the interface.
S3236.1.7 The ETS Configuration TLV "TSA Assignment Table" will be populated based on the scheduler-set configuration of the interface.
S3236.1.8 Received ETS Configuration TLVs will be processed for display purposes only, no configuration actions will be taken.
S3236.1.9 Received ETS Recommendation TLVs will be processed for display purposes only, no configuration actions will be taken.
S3236.1.10 It will be possible to enable advertisement of PFC TLVs on a per-switchport basis.
S3236.1.11 The PFC TLV "Willing" bit will always be set to 0, indicating this device is not willing to receive configuration.
S3236.1.12 The PFC TLV "MBC" bit will always be set to 0, indicating this device is capable of "bypassing MACsec processing when MACsec is disabled".
S3236.1.13 The PFC TLV "PFC cap" field will always be set to 8, indicating this device supports PFC on 8 traffic classes.
S3236.1.14 The PFC TLV "PFC Enable" field will be set based on the pfc priority configuration for the interface.
S3236.1.15 Received PFC TLVs will be processed for informational purposes only, no actions will be taken based on included configuration.

title: S3207.1.1 The MLAG service is disabled by default and must be enabled for operation of MLAG
S3207.1.2 The MLAG feature may be disabled.
S3207.1.3 The MLAG domain id may be configured
S3207.1.4 The MLAG ICCP peer address may be configured as an IPv4 address
S3207.1.5 The MLAG ICCP source address may be configured as an IPv4 address
S3207.1.6 A dynamic aggregator (LACP) may be configured to be under the control of MLAG

S3207.1.7 The number of dynamic aggregators will be limited by the maximum supported for each platform (see LID for platform limits). MLAG will not impose a limit on the number of aggregators supported.
S3207.1.8 The MLAG peer link may be configured
S3207.1.9 The ICCP keepalive interval may be configured
S3207.1.10 The ICCP session timeout may be configured
S3207.1.11 The peer-link must be configured such that it is on a different physical link from the keepalive link. This will not be enforced by software
S3207.1.12 The following must be configured for MLAG to operate:
S3207.1.13 For redundancy the MLAG peer link must be configured
S3207.1.14 For redundancy the aggregators must be configured to be part of the MLAG.
S3207.1.15 The ICCP session timeout must be larger than the keepalive interval. This will not be enforced in software.
S3207.1.16 The user is responsible for ensuring the peer link has a superset of all vlans present on all LACP aggregators participating in the MLAG.
S3207.1.17 The user is responsible for ensuring both MLAG peers have the same vlan configuration on LACP aggregators that share the same channel group id
S3207.1.18 For Layer 3 connectivity over MLAG, SAG is required.
S3207.1.19 A MLAG will comprise of 2 and only 2 peers.
S3207.1.20 MLAG will interoperate with ECMP
S3207.1.21 A Static Anycast Gateway address may be configured per VLAN interface.
3207.1.1 service mlag Turn on the MLAG service. MLAG commands are able to be run whether or not the service is turned on.
3207.1.2 no service mlag Turn off the MLAG service. MLAG will cease operating, although any existing configuration will remain in place.
3207.1.3 mlag domain <id> Create an MLAG domain and enter domain configuration mode. Domain ID can be from 1 to 4095. Only one domain can be defined at a time (this may change in future).
3207.1.4 no mlag domain <id> Destroy an MLAG domain. All configuration for the domain will be lost.

3207.1.5 keepalive-interval Define the keepalive-interval for this MLAG domain. This is the time in seconds specifying the interval at which keepalive messages will be sent between MLAG instances on different devices
3207.1.6 no keepalive-interval Set the keepalive-interval to its default value.
3207.1.7 session-timeout Define the session-timeout for this MLAG domain. This is the time in seconds specifying when an MLAG session is deemed to have failed in the absence of keepalive messages.
3207.1.8 no session-timeout Set the session-timeout to its default value.
3207.1.9 peer-address <ip address> Define the IP address of the peer MLAG device with which to establish an MLAG session.
3207.1.10 no peer-address Clear the peer address for this MLAG domain.
3207.1.11 source-address <ip address> Define the IP address of this device with respect to the esablishment of an MLAG session.
3207.1.12 no source-address Clear the source address for this MLAG domain.
3207.1.13 peer-link <link name> Define the peer link for this MLAG domain. The peer link is used to carry traffic in the event of a link to a host device going down
3207.1.14 no peer-link Clear the peer link for this MLAG domain.

3207.1.15 mlag <id> (Interface sub-command on dynamic channel-groups only). Make the specified channel-group fall under the control of the given MLAG domain. MLAG will monitor and configure the interface appropriately.

3207.1.16 no mlag <id> (Interface sub-command on dynamic channel-groups only). Remove the specified channel-group from the control of the given MLAG domain. MLAG will monitor and configure the interface appropriately.
3207.1.17 ip anycast-gateway mac MAC (Interface sub-command on VLANs). Configure anycast MAC address for Static Anycast Gateway.
3207.1.18 no ip anycast-gateway (Interface sub-command on VLANs). Deconfigure Static Anycast Gateway.
3207.1.19 show mlag state Display the state of the MLAG domain. This command is a wrapper of the shell command "mclagctl dump state".
3207.1.20 show mlag counters Display counters for the MLAG domain. This command is a wrapper of the shell command "mclagctl dump debug counters".
3207.1.21 show debug mlag shows the state of mlag debug
3207.1.22 debug mlag (msg|iccp-level(critical|err|warn|notice|info|debug)) Switch on mlag messaging debug or set ICCP log level
3207.1.23 show debug is modified to show the state of mlag debug
3207.1.24 no debug all is modified to switch off mlag messaging debug and set ICCP log level to critical
